chapter: Clubs, publishers, unions and life in Denver
title: Musicians' slang and 'axe'
summary: The interviewer recalls picking up bebop talk at sixteen; Horace says musicians had their own slang, like a hipsters' dictionary, such as 'axe' for horn.

story.theme_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band monikers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: Yeah. I can remember really the first band I went on the road with. It was when I was 16. I hadn't even graduated from high school. And it was an all black group, except for myself. And, of course, you know, this was a whole new world to me.
And it was a beebop band, actually, and I came home from that summer. I had to go back for my senior year in high school. And I had picked up all the
bebop talk and so on, and none of the kids that were my friends, you know, they didn't understand me anymore, because I was using all that jive talk.
You found a groove with them, didn't you? (Unintelligible) of the group.

Do you -- since we're talking about that, do you think that musicians, especially in those days again, that they tended to talk quite a lot in a -- using their own terminology and so on that other people didn't understand?

Oh, absolutely. As we say, that's slang. You know? In fact, Tom, somewhere around the house here I've got a book, just a small book, that it was put out by a guy that would have the musical slang in there, and he would have that expression, and then on the opposite side of the word he would actually tell you what it meant.
Define it, see. You have to actually find it, yeah.
And, oh, man, there's some funny things in there.
I think I remember that. It was called a Hipster's Dictionary or something like that.
Yeah. Yeah. And it really had some weird expressions in there, and the musicians actually used them. Just like a lot of times now a guy says, 'Hey,
man, why don't you come and sit in with us?" And the guy says, "Well, I don't have my axe with me." You know? So the guy -- other people look around and says --

What do you want an axe for? See, Then you got to stop and say, one of those things. (Unintelligible). An axe is his horn. Another guy will say, well, man, I always carry my axe with me all the time, say, well, I've got it out in the car, if you want me to go get it, you know. And then we've had people to laugh like mad, you know.
